answer: Each agent registers one saffron batch under an 85-credit bond, with an ivory strip whose shade must match the weight and crocin in the saffron register. An auditor retests a sample and checks its strip signal against the filed shade; mismatch, reuse, or missing sample burns the bond. Filing costs 33 credits first, 33+6(k-1) for the k-th, 6,027 for the 1,000th; 1,000 fakes pay 3,030,000 plus 85,000 locked. A rented-strip ring fails: each strip is keyed to one batch and sample, so a borrowed shade cannot match a second batch. An honest grower pays 33 once and recovers the bond after audit.
